content.comment_body: Could someone clarify the difference between an M flag and an IM flag? Thanks.
Hello [user_name], Is it a similar issue? IM vs. M in ladder logic programming.
Thank you, I checked that discussion but it doesn't clarify the difference—unless I missed something.

Hi [user_name], If I'm correct, an IM flag is mainly provided to act as a dummy flag, which can be used multiple times. For example, if your rung is too complex, you can split it with an IM flag at the end of one section and then use it as the initial contact in the following code.

Hi, Describing it as a dummy flag makes sense. So IM flags could also be used as relay simulations? You could use the IM coil as the end of a rung and then NO or NC contacts elsewhere to extend the logic. Thanks.
Hi again, The IM (internal memory) can be used to finish a logic operation and continue it in a new rung. Unlike M flags, you aren’t consuming the main flag resources of [product_name].
Can you explain what you mean by 'finish a logic operation'?
I meant continuing from the previous rung.
Hello, If you switch to FBD (Functional Block Diagram), these issues are much less of a concern. Regards,

Hi, This is my first time programming [product_name]. I've always worked with actual schematics and physical relays and timers. At the moment, FBD feels too advanced since I'm just translating a 1978 wiring diagram into [product_name] using ladder logic. Thanks.

Hello, Just letting you know that working in ladder logic with [product_name] can sometimes be tricky. There are several potential pitfalls, especially with copy/paste operations. Still, the choice is up to you. Regards, [user_name]

Hi, I am not copying or pasting—I'm drawing everything from scratch in a language I understand, as ladder logic looks similar to my schematic. I value your input and will consider FBD, but for now, they seem very different. Thanks.

Hello, That's fine. Usually, working with ladder logic doesn't present major issues. It might be a matter of preference, but some experts avoid ladder logic due to its limitations. If you do encounter problems, you know where to find help. Regards,
